builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: From Ripple to Boundary: Deterministic Impact Boundaries for LLM-Based Software Evolution
summary: The method replaces probabilistic semantic retrieval and text-based diffing for change impact analysis with a deterministic structural approach: design assets are formalized as a knowledge graph organized into a content-addressed Merkle DAG, and hash propagation identifies the exact code modification boundary injected into the LLM agent's context. The cost is substantial upfront engineering: teams must model their design assets as a versioned knowledge graph, maintain content addressing, and keep the graph synchronized with the codebase, plus LLM API or inference cost for the generation step itself. It can fail where design assets are undocumented or poorly structured (the common case in existing codebases), where the graph drifts from actual code, and its single-platform industrial validation may not transfer to organizations without rigorous design-driven workflows.
rationale: The approach is implementable on constrained infrastructure since the KG and Merkle DAG are cheap to build and query, but its value depends entirely on having disciplined, structured design assets, so it requires a small-scale pilot on the reader's own documentation maturity before adoption.
technique: Merkle DAG-based deterministic impact boundary for LLM code evolution
